text: Schools should allow AI tools for early-stage brainstorming but require all final drafts to be written independently, because the Stanford research on unassisted follow-up testing suggests unrestricted use measurably weakens writing skill over time. A policy that separates planning from execution captures the benefit without the cost.

Schools should allow AI tools for early-stage brainstorming but require all final drafts to be written independently, because the Stanford research on unassisted follow-up testing suggests unrestricted use measurably weakens writing skill over time. A policy that separates planning from execution captures the benefit without the cost.

AI tools should not be banned, because enforcement is nearly impossible and bans tend to punish honest students while doing little to stop determined ones. Schools have tried similar bans on other technology before with mixed results.
